arxiv-2112-09142.title: On the Formation and Interaction of Multiple Supermassive Stars in Cosmological Flows
arxiv-2112-09142.creator: Tyrone E. Woods, Samuel Patrick, Daniel J. Whalen, Alexander Heger
arxiv-2112-09142.description: Abstract Supermassive primordial stars with masses exceeding ∼ ​ 10 5 ​ M ⊙ \mathord{\sim}10^{5}\,{\mathrm{M}_{\odot}} that form in atomically cooled halos are the leading candidates for the origin of high-redshift quasars with z > 6 z>6 . Recent numerical simulations, however, find that multiple accretion disks can form within a halo, each of which can host a supermassive star.

arxiv-2210-00315.title: Using Argumentation Schemes to Model Legal Reasoning
arxiv-2210-00315.creator: Trevor Bench-Capon and Katie Atkinson
arxiv-2210-00315.description: Abstract We present argumentation schemes to model reasoning with legal cases. We provide schemes for each of the three stages that take place after the facts are established: factor ascription, issue resolution and outcome determination. The schemes are illustrated with examples from a specific legal domain, US Trade Secrets law, and the wider applicability of these schemes is discussed.

arxiv-2306-08496.title: On positive fixed points of operator of Hammerstein type with degenerate kernel and Gibbs Measures
arxiv-2306-08496.creator: I. M. Mavlonov, Kh. N. Khushvaktov, G.P. Arzikulov, F.H.Haydarov
arxiv-2306-08496.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by I. M. Mavlonov, Kh. N. Khushvaktov, G.P. Arzikulov, F.H.Haydarov. From [ 9 ] it is known that “translation-invariant Gibbs measures” of the model with an uncountable set of spin values can be described by positive fixed points of a nonlinear integral operator of Hammerstein type.

arxiv-2308-08524.title: In distributive phosphorylation catalytic constants enable non-trivial dynamics
arxiv-2308-08524.creator: Carsten Conradi, Maya Mincheva
arxiv-2308-08524.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Carsten Conradi, Maya Mincheva. Ordered distributive double phosphorylation is a recurrent motif in intracellular signaling and control. It is either sequential (where the site phosphorylated last is dephosphorylated first) or cyclic (where the site phosphorylated first is dephosphorylated first). Sequential distributive double phosphorylation has been extensively studied and an inequality involving only the catalytic constants of kinase and phosphatase is known to be sufficient for multistationarity. As multistationarity is necessary for bistability it has been argued that these constants enable bistability.

arxiv-2311-00311.title: Yang-Mills instantons as the end point of black hole evaporation
arxiv-2311-00311.creator: Pisin Chen a,b,c,d , Xiao Yan Chew e , Misao Sasaki a,f,g and Dong-han Yeom a,h,i
arxiv-2311-00311.description: Abstract Non-perturbative contributions of the Euclidean path integral are important to understand the information loss paradox. In this paper, we revisit the Yang-Mills instantons in the Einstein-Yang-Mills theory. There exists a globally regular solution that is known as the Bartnik-McKinnon solution and a black hole solution.

arxiv-2401-03163.title: An Empirical Investigation of Value-Based Multi-objective Reinforcement Learning for Stochastic Environments
arxiv-2401-03163.creator: Kewen Ding, Peter Vamplew, Cameron Foale, Richard Dazeley
arxiv-2401-03163.description: Abstract One common approach to solve multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) problems is to extend conventional Q-learning by using vector Q-values in combination with a utility function. However issues can arise with this approach in the context of stochastic environments, particularly when optimising for the Scalarised Expected Reward (SER) criterion.

arxiv-2401-14134.title: The Shizuta - Kawashima Condition for the Barotropic SHTC Two Fluid Model
arxiv-2401-14134.creator: Ferdinand Thein
arxiv-2401-14134.description: Abstract Recently the barotropic two fluid model belonging to the class of symmetric hyperbolic thermodynamically compatible (SHTC) systems was studied in detail in [ 13 ] . There the question was raised whether the dissipative structure introduced by the source terms satisfies the Shizuta - Kawashima condition.

arxiv-2510-17820.title: The Standard Model of the Retina
arxiv-2510-17820.creator: Markus Meister
arxiv-2510-17820.description: Abstract 1 Abstract The scientific study of the retina has reached a remarkable state of completion. We can now explain many aspects of early visual processing based on a relatively simple model of neural circuitry in the retina. The same model, with different parameters, produces a great diversity of neural computations.

arxiv-2512-21870.title: Nascent biofilms on soft surfaces
arxiv-2512-21870.creator: Garima Rani, G. H. Philipp Nguyen, René Wittmann, Hartmut Löwen, Anupam Sengupta, Email: hartmut.loewen@uni-duesseldorf.de, anupam.sengupta@uni.lu
arxiv-2512-21870.description: Abstract Soft surfaces, spanning vastly different environmental and biomedical settings, are frequently colonised by surface-associated bacteria. Yet, how soft surfaces govern bacterial dynamics and their self-organisation into colonies remains poorly understood. Using experiments and agent-based modelling, we report the self-organisation of bacterial cells into nascent biofilms on soft substrates.

pmc-10744144.title: Indenopyrene and Blue-Light Co-Exposure Impairs the Tightly Controlled Activation of Xenobiotic Metabolism in Retinal Pigment Epithelial Cells: A Mechanism for Synergistic Toxicity
pmc-10744144.creator: Corinne Zinflou, Patrick J. Rochette
pmc-10744144.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). High energy visible (HEV) blue light is an increasing source of concern for visual health. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), a group of compounds found in high concentrations in smokers and polluted environments, accumulate in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). HEV absorption by indeno [1,2,3-cd]pyrene (IcdP), a common PAH, synergizes their toxicities and promotes degenerative changes in RPE cells comparable to the ones observed in age-related macular degeneration.

pmc-11345102.title: Lingual Abscess in an Adult Patient With Pierre Robin Sequence: A Case Report
pmc-11345102.creator: Hiram H Plata-Huerta, Astrid E Rosero-Castillo, Jose Luis Trevino Gonzalez
pmc-11345102.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A lingual abscess is a rare but serious infection within the tongue parenchyma, posing significant risks due to potential airway obstruction. Despite advancements in oral hygiene and antibiotics, timely diagnosis and treatment are critical to prevent severe complications. In this case, we report a 29-year-old male with Pierre Robin sequence (PRS) who presented with a four-day history of severe tongue pain, swelling, decreased appetite, and fever, without any reported trauma.

Several pharmaceutical companies are advancing oral GLP-1 RAs to improve adherence and patient acceptability in the treatment of T2DM and obesity.

pmc-12717270.title: Redox properties of quercetin iron II complex with enhanced antioxidant and antiviral activities
pmc-12717270.creator: Sara E. Abdel Hameed, Weam M. Abou El-Maaty, Esam A. Gomaa, Fathi S. Awad
pmc-12717270.description: Quercetin is a naturally occurring flavonoid widely recognized for its potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer effects. However, its clinical application is limited by low water solubility and poor bioavailability. In this study, the complexation of quercetin with iron (II) ions was systematically investigated through electrochemical, spectroscopic, biological, and computational techniques to improve its physicochemical and pharmacological performance.

pmc-13084919.title: Occupational exposure to toxic particles and risk of pulmonary sarcoidosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13084919.creator: Nada Kotti, Amel Kchaou, Walid Feki, Asma Daoud, Feriel Dhouib, Nehla Rmadi, Wiem Feki, Mouna Snoussi, Rim Kammoun, Faten Omrane, Slim Charfi, Nadia Moussa, Rym Sahnoun, Mounira Hajjaji, Kaouthar Jmal Hammami
pmc-13084919.description: IntroductionThe onset of sarcoidosis is likely the result of a complex genetic-environment-immunological interaction. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify occupational toxic particles associated with an increased risk of developing pulmonary sarcoidosis.MethodsPublications in English, published from January 2000 to January 2025, were searched in PubMed, Scopus and JSTOR. The risk of bias was assessed for all included studies.

pmc-13202906.title: Acute inferior STEMI in a unique setting: case report on anomalous circumflex and multivessel coronary artery disease
pmc-13202906.creator: Hesham Salah Eldin Taha, Mirna Mamdouh Shaker
pmc-13202906.description: BackgroundThe majority of coronary artery anomalies are harmless and asymptomatic. However, in rare cases, they have been linked to myocardial ischemia and sudden cardiac death. One of the most frequently occurring coronary anomalies is the aberrant origin of the circumflex coronary artery (Cx) from the right coronary sinus.

pmc-13351000.title: Biomimetic-voltage nitride-enhanced memristor arrays for femtojoule in-memory biosignal processing
pmc-13351000.creator: Zijian Wang, Zhejia Zhang, Guobin Zhang, Xuemeng Fan, Pengtao Li, Baicheng Zhu, Yi Tong, Panpan Zhang, Dawei Gao, Bin Yu, Jiuren Zhou, Qing Wan, Yishu Zhang
pmc-13351000.description: Edge audio recognition demands extreme energy efficiency and noise resilience. Conventional separate denoising and recognition modules incur high overhead and latency, hindering deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. Inspired by biological audition, here we show a memristor-based neuromorphic system that monolithically integrates on-chip audio denoising and recognition.

pmc-13411838.title: ACSL5 programs fatty acid metabolism and mitochondrial fitness to sustain pathogenic T cells and exacerbate Sjögren's syndrome
pmc-13411838.creator: Xinyi Ren, Junhao Yin, Xinyi Ma, Jiabao Xu, Changyu Chen, Lele He, Ruowen Zhao, Yucheng Xu, Yiping Pu, Baoli Wang, Jiayao Fu, Lingyan Zheng
pmc-13411838.description: Emerging evidence has shown that fatty acid metabolism is closely associated with autoreactive T cells in autoimmunity, but its function in Sjögren's syndrome (SS) is still unclear. Here, we identified acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 5 (ACSL5) as a metabolic checkpoint that drives pathogenic T-cell responses in SS.

uslaw-usc-t16-s4903.title: 16 U.S.C. § 4903 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t16-s4903.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s4903.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 69 (Wild Exotic Bird Conservation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this chapter— (1) The term “Convention” means the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, as amended, signed in Washington on March 3, 1973, and the Appendices thereto. (2) The term “exotic bird”— (A) means any live or dead.

uslaw-usc-t43-s485h7.title: 43 U.S.C. § 485h–7 — Amendment of repayment contract for payment of annual installments in two parts
uslaw-usc-t43-s485h7.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s485h7.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 12 (Reclamation And Irrigation Of Lands By Federal Government); Subchapter X (Payment Of Construction Charges). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In any repayment contract which provides for payment of construction charges by single annual installments, the Secretary may by agreement with the contracting organization amend such contract to provide for the payment of such.
